result.summary: This unit is the zig-gobject bindings package: build.zig declares Zig modules for the GNOME libraries and links them via pkg-config, and gdkpixbuf2.zig is GIR-generated extern bindings for gdk-pixbuf. I checked the build script, the package manifest and the gdkpixbuf2 source for build-time execution, fetching, embedded payloads, load-time side effects and hooking. I found nothing beyond the documented, opt-in glib-compile-resources helper.

findings.title: Build helper invokes glib-compile-resources
findings.detail: build.zig's CompileResources helper runs the system command `glib-compile-resources` and compiles a helper executable from build/build_gresources_xml.zig, but only when a dependent build uses addCompileResources/buildCompileResources. This is the documented purpose of the helper. The rest of build.zig only declares modules and links system libraries via pkg-config.

findings.title: No remote dependencies
findings.detail: build.zig.zon has no active dependencies. The only dependency, a zig_autodoc fork, is commented out, so nothing is fetched at build time.

findings.title: Generated bindings only
findings.detail: gdkpixbuf2.zig is a machine-generated set of extern declarations and thin wrappers for the gdk-pixbuf C library. It contains no initialisers, comptime side effects, embedded data, network access or process execution. The extern g_object_ref/unref declarations reuse GObject symbols with typed pointers, which is normal for GIR-generated bindings.
